notes: Perfect claim overlap (Jaccard=1.0) on S259A mutant experiments. Both evaluators agree the mutational analysis provides strong evidence for MCU pore structure-function relationships and RuR sensitivity mechanisms.

High claim overlap (Jaccard=0.769) on MCU knockdown experiments. Both agree knockdown data provide strong evidence for MCU's role. Peer review includes C4 and C52 not in LLM R1, but overall assessment aligns.

Strong claim overlap (Jaccard=0.714) on MCU overexpression experiments. Both evaluators accept the overexpression data as valid evidence. Peer review includes C43 not in LLM R2, but conclusions align.

Moderate claim overlap (Jaccard=0.6) on main conclusion that MCU is pore-forming subunit. Both strongly support this conclusion based on converging evidence. Peer review includes C47 while LLM includes C52, but overall agreement is clear.

Good claim overlap (Jaccard=0.625) on voltage-clamp methodology and IMiCa properties. LLM finds methodology fully validated; peer reviewers request protocol clarification but implicitly accept data validity as part of 'strong evidence.' Both ultimately support the claims.

No direct claim overlap, but both address methodological validation. LLM R5 focuses on biophysical properties validation (C28-C32, C62, C67-C68), while peer R7 praises patch-clamp methodology (C18-C19, C49-C51). Both positive but evaluate different methodological aspects.

No claim overlap. LLM R5 addresses voltage-clamp validation of IMiCa properties; peer R5 expresses uncertainty about mitoplast morphology image quality (C64-C66). Different experimental aspects evaluated with divergent assessments.

Minimal claim overlap (Jaccard=0.067, only C28). LLM R1 focuses on knockdown validation; peer R6 on voltage protocol methodology. Both support their respective claims but address largely different experimental components.

Minimal claim overlap (Jaccard=0.059, only C4). LLM R2 focuses on overexpression experiments; peer R1 provides broader assessment including knockdown. Both support MCU evidence but evaluate different experimental subsets.
Minimal claim overlap (Jaccard=0.067, only C52). LLM R4 addresses overall conclusion; peer R1 focuses on knockdown/overexpression evidence. Both support claims but at different levels of synthesis.

Minimal claim overlap (Jaccard=0.071, only C43). LLM R3 addresses S259A mutant; peer R2 addresses overexpression. Both support their respective claims but evaluate distinct experimental manipulations.
